 ● The Last Light of Karrow Rock                                                                                       ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   Elias Marrow had kept the light at Karrow Rock for thirty-one years, and in that time he had learned that the sea   ┃
   never repeated itself. It only seemed to.                                                                           ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   Each evening, an hour before sunset, he climbed the one hundred and twelve steps to the lantern room. He counted    ┃
   them without meaning to, the way other men count heartbeats. At the top he wiped the great lens with a soft cloth,  █
   checked the rotation mechanism, and waited for the sun to touch the horizon. Then he lit the lamp, and Karrow Rock  █
   spoke to the dark the way it had since 1887: two long flashes, one short, then a pause of twelve seconds.           █
                                                                                                                       █
   Nobody had told him this would probably be the last winter.                                                         █
                                                                                                                       █
   He learned it from a letter. The envelope was thin and official, delivered by the supply boat on a grey Tuesday in  █
   October. The Coastal Authority regretted to inform him that Karrow Rock would be automated by spring. A sensor      █
   array would replace him, and a solar panel would replace the oil he still insisted on keeping in reserve. His       █
   pension would be generous. He was thanked for his service.                                                          █
                                                                                                                       █
   Elias read it twice, folded it into quarters, and put it in                                                         █
